title: 递归自我改进走到哪一步了?「AI 改进 AI」的分层体检(深入版) — BigCat Deep Research
title_en: How Far Has Recursive Self-Improvement Actually Gone? A Layer-by-Layer Inspection of "AI Improving AI" (Deep Dive) — BigCat Deep Research

questions.question: 这份深度研究用什么标准判断一个系统是否在「递归自我改进」？
options: AI 撰写了实验室绝大部分代码，使整体研发速度远快于没有 AI 的情形
AI 能够自行修改自己的 prompt、工具和 agent 脚手架代码
有证据显示它让下一轮改进本身变得更快或更大，而且这种效应逐轮累积
AI 在某个公开基准上的表现超过了人类工程师搭建的基线
questions.explanation: 文章区分「改进了产出」和「改进了改进能力」，只有「改进了改进能力」且逐轮累积才算。它援引 Anthropic 自己的 RSP：即便 AI 让进步速度远快于反事实，只要速率恒定或放缓就不算越过阈值——看的是加速度，不是被 AI 托住的高速度。能改自己的脚手架只是 L1 的活动，本身不等于递归。
questions.question_en: What criterion does this deep-research report use to decide whether a system is undergoing recursive self-improvement?
options_en: AI writes most of a lab's code, making R&D far faster than it would be without AI
AI can modify its own prompts, tools and agent scaffolding code
Evidence that it makes the next round of improvement itself faster or larger, with the effect compounding round over round
AI beats a human-engineered baseline on some public benchmark
questions.explanation_en: The report separates improving outputs from improving the ability to improve; only the latter, compounding across rounds, counts. It cites Anthropic's own RSP: even if AI makes progress far faster than the counterfactual, a constant or slowing rate doesn't cross the threshold — what matters is acceleration, not AI-sustained speed. Editing one's own scaffolding is just L1 activity, not recursion by itself.

questions.question: 根据 Darwin Gödel Machine 的消融实验，它的性能增益主要来自哪里？
options: 人类专家对每一轮改写提案的人工筛选
开放式的档案搜索，而不是改进者本身在变强
基础模型在自我改进过程中被持续地微调更新
自我修改让每一轮改进来得越来越快、越来越大
questions.explanation: 消融显示去掉自改后分数仍保留大半，去掉开放式档案则在 Polyglot 上原地不动；基础模型全程冻结。文章总结 L1 的第一个共同形状就是「增益来自搜索，不来自改进者变强」。
questions.question_en: According to the Darwin Gödel Machine's ablations, where did most of its performance gains come from?
options_en: Human experts manually screening each round's rewrite proposals
The open-ended archive search, not the improver itself getting better
The base model being continually fine-tuned during self-improvement
Self-modification making each round of improvement faster and larger
questions.explanation_en: The ablations show that removing self-modification keeps most of the gain, while removing the open-ended archive leaves Polyglot flat; the base model stays frozen throughout. The report's first common pattern for L1 is that gains come from search, not from the improver getting stronger.

questions.question: 关于 L2「模型自己出题、自己打分」这一类自我改进，文章汇总的证据显示什么？
options: DeepSeek-R1 的推理跃进证明了纯自打分能持续推高能力
自打分的进步稳定可持续，只是速度慢于有硬裁判的方法
模型规模越大，能持续自我改进的轮数就越多，呈现出复利
没有新信息时通常两三轮就饱和，缺少外部裁判时还会退化甚至崩溃
questions.explanation: Song 等发现无新信息时迭代自改「两三轮就饱和，与模型能力无关」；规模变大的是单轮可收割的余量，不是轮数。R-Zero 的伪标签准确率逐轮下降，SRT 甚至突然崩溃。R1 的奖励来自硬裁判而非自打分，文章特意把这个混淆挪开。
questions.question_en: For L2 self-improvement — models setting and grading their own problems — what does the report's evidence show?
options_en: DeepSeek-R1's reasoning leap proves pure self-grading can keep pushing capability up
Self-grading gains are steady and sustainable, just slower than methods with hard verifiers
Bigger models can sustain more rounds of self-improvement, producing a compounding effect
Without new information it usually saturates within two or three rounds, and without an external judge it degrades or even collapses
questions.explanation_en: Song et al. found iterative self-improvement without new information "saturates after two or three rounds, regardless of the model's capacity"; scale grows the harvestable margin per round, not the number of rounds. R-Zero's pseudo-label accuracy fell each round, and SRT collapsed outright. R1's rewards came from hard verifiers, not self-grading — a confusion the report explicitly clears up.
